A2.evidence: Looked for a metadata record persisting independently of the code files. None: supplement-only deposit with no independent record, so if the supplementary files were withdrawn no software metadata would remain. Row 6 sets A2 = 0 for supplement-only deposits.

F1.evidence: The analysis scripts - the principal code artefact - are distributed as a supplement of the article: "The script used to run all validation analyses is available in the supplementary information" (§2.3.3) and "The script used to run all case study tests is available in the supplementary information" (§2.4), with Appendix A pointing to https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jas.2023.105921. F4.evidence: Looked for indexing in a software registry (Zenodo, CRAN, Software Heritage, JOSS). The paper names no repository or archive for the scripts - they exist only as supplementary information; pack shows no such record. Row 6: F4 = 0.

I1.evidence: The code is expressed in a formal, open, broadly applicable language, explicitly named with version: "All analyses were undertaken in 'R' version 4.3.0. I2.evidence: Looked for FAIR vocabularies applied to the software (CodeMeta terms, SPDX identifiers in machine-readable metadata, a controlled software-metadata schema). I3.evidence: Looked for qualified, typed references from the code to other resources by PID (e.g. dependency declarations citing package DOIs, 'uses software [DOI]'). No package dependencies, no dependency file, and no typed links are reported anywhere in the paper; method sources are cited narratively in the article text only.

R1_1.evidence: No separate licence is stated for the supplementary script, so under the R1.1 supplement rule the article licence governs: "This is an open access article under the CC BY license (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)". R1_2.evidence: Looked for code provenance: authorship of the script (the CRediT statement lists no Software role - "Alastair Key: Conceptualization, Data curation, Formal analysis, Investigation, Methodology, Validation, Writing"), version history, dependency versions, or random seeds for the stochastic procedures. The paper reports analytical parameters ("One thousand iterations of each process were performed"; k = 5, 10, 20, 30) and the R version 4.3.0 only - no seed, no package versions, no code versioning or derivation history.

R1_3.evidence: Looked for the qualifying code routes: package structure, CITATION.cff, CodeMeta, or community review (CRAN, JOSS, rOpenSci). None - the artefact is a loose script in publisher supplementary information with no packaging, citation file, or peer-reviewed software venue.

A2.evidence: Looked for a metadata record that would survive the data becoming unavailable (tombstone, repository metadata commitment). F1.evidence: Data-bearing supplement is distributed under the article DOI: "Supplementary data to this article can be found online at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jas.2023.105921" (Appendix A); supplementary tables are cited in-text (e.g. "Supplementary Table 3", "Supplementary Figs. 1 and 2"). Pack confirms the DOI is registered and resolving (http_status 200). Instrument F1 credits the article DOI where the artefact is distributed as that article's supplement.

F2.evidence: Looked for an independent, artefact-level metadata record for the data. Platform table Row 6 (publisher supplement of a Crossref-registered article): "NO independent metadata record ... hence F2 = F3 = F4 = 0".

F3.evidence: F3 is strictly artefact-level. F4.evidence: Looked for indexing of the data in a searchable registry (Zenodo, DataCite, domain repository). None named in the paper; pack records only Crossref indexing of the article. I1.evidence: Looked for a statement of the file format or knowledge representation of the deposited data. The paper never names a format for the supplementary tables; in-article data appear only as typeset summary tables (Tables 1-7: "Mean, Minimum, OLE Minimum, Maximum, OLE Maximum"), which are not machine-actionable. I2.evidence: Looked for controlled vocabularies or ontologies with PIDs (ARIADNEplus, CIDOC-CRM, Getty AAT, PeriodO). None used. Variables are ad hoc morphometric field names defined in-text: "Flake length (mm), width (mm), thickness (mm) and mass (g)"; "*Refinement is used here to describe the relative thickness of a tool (thickness divided by breadth)" - a locally defined term, not a vocabulary term.

I3.evidence: Looked for qualified, typed PID references from the data artefact to other resources. The article's reference list cites source studies (e.g. "Data are derived from Buchanan and Hamilton's (2021) study") but these are narrative citations in the article, not typed relations (isDerivedFrom / isSupplementTo) carried in any data-artefact metadata; no such record exists (pack holds only the article record).

R1.evidence: Each dataset is described with a plurality of relevant attributes in §2.4: provenance, chronology, sample size, variables and recording method - e.g. "We use length (mm), breadth (mm), thickness (mm) and mass (g) data recorded from each core following the method outlined by de la Pena and Wadley (2014)"; "we limit the present case study to the whole flakes excavated from MIS 15 sediments in the 2020 season (n = 173)"; Table 1 gives full descriptive statistics (Mean, SD, CV, Minimum, Maximum) for the validation assemblages.

R1_1.evidence: Licence identified as CC BY 4.0: "This is an open access article under the CC BY license (http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)". Per the R1.1 supplement rule, absent a separate supplement licence the article's licence extends to publisher-hosted supplements. Pack corroborates (licences include "cc-by-4.0"; licence_conflicts entry records paper_asserted "CC BY" with "conflict": false).

R1_2.evidence: Detailed provenance is documented for the data: origin and collection context ("500 replica Acheulean handaxes were produced by Key and Lycett (2017) on British flint ... The replica assemblages were produced before the present study was conceived, and thus serve as a blind test"), recording methods per case study ("The metric data were recorded in centimetres from plan-view and profile-view digital images"), and processing ("we decided to run a series of additional analyses for the microlith sample that were also able to include duplicate records ... We repeated the OLE procedure with randomised values for 1000 iterations").

R1_3.evidence: Looked for deposit-level standards: a generic metadata schema (DataCite, Dublin Core), a domain schema or vocabulary (ARIADNEplus, CIDOC-CRM), or deposit in an accredited domain repository whose ingest enforces its standard (Row 4). None present - the data sit in a publisher supplement with no metadata record. The methodological standards used (OLE modelling per Roberts and Solow 2003; R 4.3.0) expressly do not qualify under the R1.3 boundary.
